Warm volcanic neutrals, magma-orange accents, and a dense, link-heavy, code-heavy layout language built for technical docs (Astro-style hub/detail pages, left navigation, API reference tables, and syntax-styled code blocks). Every page on this site is built from these components and tokens. Use them rather than writing custom markup or styling — hand-rolled equivalents break visual consistency and will not pick up future design-system changes. ## Components ### alert Callout box for notes, warnings, and danger/breaking-change notices inside docs content. | Parameter | Type | Default | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `variant` | string | `info` | One of info, success, warning, danger. | | `title` | string | `Note` | Callout heading. | | `body_html` | html | `This endpoint is deprecated in favor of ` | Callout body content, may include inline links. | **Usage:** variant must match one of the fixed CSS suffixes: info, success, warning, danger. Any other value falls back to the default neutral alert border. ### card Link tile used on hub pages to point at guides, API endpoints, SDKs, or concepts. | Parameter | Type | Default | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `href` | string | `/guides/building-your-first-pipeline` | Destination URL. | | `tag` | string | `Guide` | Short category label shown above the title. | | `title` | string | `Building your first pipeline` | Card title. | | `description` | string | `Learn how to assemble your first data pi` | One or two sentence summary. | **Usage:** Use one card component call per tile on hub/index pages such as Guides hub, API Reference hub, and SDKs hub. ### chip Small inline badge used for version tags and status labels (e.g. v2, Beta, Deprecated). | Parameter | Type | Default | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `label` | string | `v2` | Chip text. | | `variant` | string | `primary` | One of primary, success, warning, danger, info, or omit for neutral. | **Usage:** variant maps directly to a fixed CSS class suffix; Events endpoint v3

Query and replay events that have flowed through a pipeline. Base URL: https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v3.

List events

GET /v3/pipelines/{pipeline_id}/events — cursor-paginated, filterable by type and occurred_at range.

Name Type Required Description
typestringNoFilter to a single event type, e.g. order.created.
sincestringNoISO-8601 timestamp lower bound on occurred_at.
untilstringNoISO-8601 timestamp upper bound on occurred_at. New in v3.
cursorstringNoOpaque pagination cursor from a previous response's next_cursor.
event.json json 
{
  "id": "evt_8f2c1a90",
  "type": "order.created",
  "occurred_at": "2026-08-18T09:12:44Z",
  "payload": { "order_id": "ord_4471" },
  "retention_until": "2026-09-18T09:12:44Z"
}

Replay a dead-lettered event

POST /v3/events/{id}/replay — re-runs an event that exhausted its retries from where it was dead-lettered. See the Handling errors & retries guide for when to use this versus reprocessing an entire time range.

Platform events

Lifecycle notifications like pipeline.started and connector.error are not returned by this endpoint — subscribe to them through the Webhooks endpoint instead.

Event retention (v3 feature)

v3 adds transparent event retention tracking. Each event includes a retention_until timestamp showing when it will be purged. This is determined by the pipeline's retention_days setting. Use the new until parameter to query events within compliance windows.

Migration guide (v2 → v3) Required

v2 support has ended. You must migrate to v3 immediately. v3 ships with event retention configuration and compliance-focused query features. The endpoints are straightforward to upgrade.

v2 support withdrawn

v2 of the Events endpoint is no longer supported as of this release. All v2 clients must upgrade to v3 to continue using the platform. Requests to v2 endpoints will be rejected.

What's new in v3

v3 adds critical compliance and observability features:

  • retention_days — Control how long events are kept in each pipeline (1–365 days, default: 30). Allows fine-grained control over data lifecycle and compliance obligations without blanket org-wide policies.
  • retention_until — Every event now includes a transparent retention deadline, letting you query events within compliance windows.
  • until parameter — Query events up to an upper timestamp bound, in addition to the existing since lower bound.

Update client code

This is a required change. Update your base URLs and optionally add retention_days to any pipeline creation requests:

diff diff 
- POST https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2/pipelines
+ POST https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v3/pipelines

  {
    "name": "ingest-orders",
    "source_connector_id": "conn_pg_orders",
    "destination_connector_id": "conn_snowflake_dw",
+   "retention_days": 90
  }

- GET https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2/pipelines/backfill-events/events?since=2026-08-01T00:00:00Z
+ GET https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v3/pipelines/backfill-events/events?since=2026-08-01T00:00:00Z&until=2026-08-31T23:59:59Z

- POST https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2/events/evt_abc123/replay
+ POST https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v3/events/evt_abc123/replay

New compliance features

Per-pipeline retention policies let you handle mixed data classifications in a single workspace:

  • PII pipelines — Set retention_days: 7 to comply with short data minimization windows.
  • Analytics pipelines — Set retention_days: 365 for longer historical context.
  • Audit logs — Set retention_days: 30 to meet standard compliance standards.

v3 enforces retention at the pipeline level, so different data flows can have independent lifespans. Query the retention_until field on events to confirm your compliance window.

Migration timeline

v2 is no longer supported. Upgrade your integrations immediately. All v2 requests will be rejected.

No backward compatibility

Unlike earlier migrations, v3 requires a URL change. There is no v2 compatibility mode in v3. Update all client base URLs from /v2 to /v3.

Migration notes

  • The retention_days default is 30 days, matching the implicit v2 behavior. If v2 pipelines retained events beyond 30 days, set an explicit retention_days value on upgrade.
  • SDK clients must update the base URL — cached v2 URLs will fail. Clear any cached configuration and redeploy.
  • The new until parameter on list events is optional — omit it to get all events from since to present.
  • Every event response now includes retention_until, which you can use for compliance audits and data governance workflows.

Still stuck?

Common migration issues are covered in Troubleshooting / FAQ. Or contact support if you hit any blockers.

Events endpoint v3

Query and replay events that have flowed through a pipeline. Base URL: https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v3. Upgrading from v2?

List events

GET /v3/pipelines/{pipeline_id}/events — cursor-paginated, filterable by type and occurred_at range.

Name Type Required Description
typestringNoFilter to a single event type, e.g. order.created.
sincestringNoISO-8601 timestamp lower bound on occurred_at.
untilstringNoISO-8601 timestamp upper bound on occurred_at. New in v3.
cursorstringNoOpaque pagination cursor from a previous response's next_cursor.
event.json json 
{
  "id": "evt_8f2c1a90",
  "type": "order.created",
  "occurred_at": "2026-08-18T09:12:44Z",
  "payload": { "order_id": "ord_4471" },
  "retention_until": "2026-09-18T09:12:44Z"
}

Replay a dead-lettered event

POST /v3/events/{id}/replay — re-runs an event that exhausted its retries from where it was dead-lettered. See the Handling errors & retries guide for when to use this versus reprocessing an entire time range.

Platform events

Lifecycle notifications like pipeline.started and connector.error are not returned by this endpoint — subscribe to them through the Webhooks endpoint instead.

Event retention (v3 feature)

v3 adds transparent event retention tracking. Each event includes a retention_until timestamp showing when it will be purged. This is determined by the pipeline's retention_days setting. Use the new until parameter to query events within compliance windows.
